classification_note: The fix commit describes an invalid buffer access during OOM handling. In the saved witness, that control bug manifests as a MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value after `OT::apply_lookup()` continues past a failed `buffer->move_to()` and a later nested coverage lookup consumes a glyph id from unwritten `buffer->info`; Stage 01 does not preserve which earlier cursor-setting transition left the reused cursor on that slot.

analysis_state.reason: Stage 01 reproduced the MSan crash in `bsearch<unsigned int>`, and the staged diff closes the local root cause at `OT::apply_lookup`: the return value of `buffer->move_to(match_positions[idx])` is ignored, so a `move_to()` allocation failure still falls through to `c->recurse(...)` on unchanged cursor state. The MSan allocation origin independently ties the consumed value to unwritten `hb_buffer_t::enlarge()` storage. What the saved artifacts do not record, and `run_flags.json` forbids instrumenting, is the exact earlier cursor-setting transition that made that unchanged cursor alias the unwritten slot later read at `ContextFormat3::apply:1505`.

bug_description.original: An invalid buffer access occurs in out-of-memory (OOM) situations, potentially leading to a security vulnerability.
bug_description.normalized: During the second `hb_shape()` call, `hb-fuzzer` copies the witness's last 64 bytes into `text32[16]` and feeds them to `hb_buffer_add_utf32()`. `hb_buffer_t::enlarge()` can grow `buffer->info` with `realloc`, and `hb_buffer_t::add()` initializes only the 16 live `hb_glyph_info_t` entries, leaving spare tail capacity unwritten. Separately, the attacker-controlled font reaches GSUB `ContextFormat3::apply()`, which materializes `LookupRecord[]` and `match_positions[]` for recursive `apply_lookup()` processing. At line 987, vulnerable `OT::apply_lookup()` calls `buffer->move_to(match_positions[idx])` but does not check the boolean result; if `move_to()` hits its internal allocation-failure path, the same iteration still falls through to line 990 and recurses on unchanged cursor state. The saved MSan stack proves nested `ContextFormat3::apply` / `OT::apply_lookup` recursion reaches line 1505, then `CoverageFormat1::get_coverage()`, then `bsearch<unsigned int>`, and the saved allocation origin shows the consumed uninitialized glyph id came from the `hb_buffer_t::enlarge()` allocation. The exact earlier cursor-setting transition that made the unchanged cursor alias that unwritten `buffer->info` slot is not preserved in Stage 01 artifacts, so this repaired GT keeps that bridge explicit instead of asserting a more specific stale-cursor witness mechanism than the saved evidence supports.

source.description: First project-side statement on the crashing path that materializes one attacker-controlled UTF-32 codepoint from the witness's trailing 64-byte text block into a live `buffer->info` slot of the second shaping buffer.
source.value_from: In `hb-fuzzer`, if `size > sizeof(text32)`, the input's last 64 bytes are copied into `text32[16]` and passed to `hb_buffer_add_utf32()`. `hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf32_t<true> >()` decodes those 16 attacker-controlled codepoints and reaches `hb_buffer_t::add()` before the crashing second `hb_shape()` call.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSan allocation origin. During the second shaping block, `realloc` grows `buffer->info`; any tail `hb_glyph_info_t` slots beyond later live writes remain uninitialized until a later store touches them.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved origin stack is `hb_buffer_t::enlarge -> ensure -> hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf32_t<true> > -> hb_buffer_add_utf32 -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`. Stage 01 does not preserve which later cursor-setting transition made `buffer->idx` alias one of these unwritten slots.

root_cause.description: Unchecked `move_to()` call. When `move_to()` needs internal buffer movement and hits allocation failure, `apply_lookup()` ignores the false return and still falls through to recurse on unchanged cursor state.
root_cause.note: The fixing diff changes this exact call site to `if (unlikely (!buffer->move_to (match_positions[idx]))) break;`, preventing line 990 from dispatching a recursive sublookup after the failed reposition. The exact earlier cursor-setting step that made the unchanged cursor alias the later unwritten slot is not preserved in Stage 01 artifacts.

sink.description: MSan crash site. `x` is the glyph id forwarded from the nested coverage lookup, and the compare/branch at line 1055 is where MemorySanitizer reports the poisoned read.
sink.note: The saved crash trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `bsearch<unsigned int>` at `src/hb-open-type-private.hh:1055:11`, with callers `get_coverage`, `OT::Coverage::get_coverage`, and `OT::ContextFormat3::apply`.

parser_admitted.code: return_trace (context_apply_lookup (c, glyphCount, (const USHORT *) (coverageZ + 1), lookupCount, lookupRecord, lookup_context));
parser_admitted.description: The staged font reaches recursive GSUB ContextFormat3 processing. The saved crash stack shows two `ContextFormat3::apply` frames and two `OT::apply_lookup` frames before the sink.

utf32_text_loaded.description: The saved MSan allocation origin comes from the second shaping block, where `hb-fuzzer` copies the input's last 64 bytes into `text32[16]` and feeds them through `hb_buffer_add_utf32()` before calling `hb_shape()`.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, and `trace_feedback.json` does not request the bounded exception, so Stage 02 may not instrument which earlier cursor-setting operation left `buffer->idx` on the unwritten `buffer->info` slot later read at `ContextFormat3::apply:1505`.

The saved MSan artifacts close three local facts: `hb_buffer_t::enlarge()` allocated the uninitialized heap region, the crash-side read chain is `ContextFormat3::apply -> CoverageFormat1::get_coverage -> bsearch<unsigned int>`, and the fixing diff guards the unchecked `buffer->move_to(match_positions[idx])` call. They do not record which prior `move_to()` / recursive-lookup transition positioned the unchanged cursor on the unwritten slot.
Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable build. `patch_resolves` is set from the exact fixing diff at the root-cause call site, not from a saved fixed-build rerun.

coarse_trace.summary: The second shaping buffer grows via `realloc`, and only the 16 live UTF-32 glyph slots are initialized afterward, leaving spare `buffer->info` capacity unwritten.
The attacker-controlled GSUB ContextFormat3 subtable materializes `LookupRecord[]` and match positions that drive recursive sublookups.

A `buffer->move_to(match_positions[idx])` failure inside `apply_lookup()` is unchecked, so the same iteration still recurses on unchanged cursor state; the staged artifacts do not record which earlier cursor-setting step made that reused cursor alias the later unwritten slot.
The nested sublookup rereads `buffer->cur().codepoint`; MSan ties the consumed value to unwritten `buffer->info` storage, but the exact cursor bridge into that slot is not preserved.
Coverage lookup forwards that glyph id into binary search, where MSan reports `use-of-uninitialized-value`.

fine_trace.note: MSan allocation origin. During the second `hb_shape()` call, `hb_buffer_add_utf32()` can grow `buffer->info` for the 16-codepoint trailing UTF-32 block. `realloc` yields raw `hb_glyph_info_t` capacity; any slots beyond later live writes remain uninitialized.
Each decoded codepoint zeroes and fills only the current live `info[len]` slot and then increments `len`; spare capacity beyond the 16 `text32` entries stays unwritten.
Font-controlled ContextFormat3 materializes `LookupRecord[]`; later `sequenceIndex` and `lookupListIndex` fields choose which matched position to move to and which recursive lookup to dispatch.
After the outer coverage check succeeds, `match_input()` records the matched glyph positions for the current context into `match_positions[]` on the shared buffer.
`apply_lookup()` converts those matched positions from current input indices into the output-buffer coordinate space later passed to `buffer->move_to()`.

The current `LookupRecord` selects which matched glyph position this iteration wants to reposition to. The staged artifacts do not record which loop index `i` or concrete `sequenceIndex` value was used on the witness, only that this record survives the `idx >= count` and self-recursion skips.

Root-cause call site. Vulnerable `apply_lookup()` invokes `buffer->move_to(match_positions[idx])` but does not branch on the boolean result before proceeding to line 990. The fix wraps this exact statement in `if (unlikely (!buffer->move_to (match_positions[idx]))) break;`.

On this path `have_output` is active. At loop entry `!buffer->in_error` already held, so the supported failure mode here is an internal allocation failure in `make_room_for()` or `shift_forward()`. In either branch `move_to()` returns false before updating `idx` or `out_len`.

Despite step 8's false return, vulnerable code still computes `orig_len` from current state and calls `c->recurse(lookupRecord[i].lookupListIndex)` on the same shared `c->buffer`. This is the sink-reaching control bug the patch stops.

The nested `ContextFormat3` sublookup immediately reads `c->buffer->cur().codepoint` at the cursor reused by step 9. The saved MSan stack proves this nested `ContextFormat3::apply` / `OT::apply_lookup` recursion, and the saved allocation origin attributes the consumed uninitialized value to step 1, but the staged source does not preserve which earlier cursor-setting transition made this cursor alias an unwritten `buffer->info` slot.
CoverageFormat1 forwards that glyph id into binary search over the font-backed coverage array.
MSan sink. `glyphArray.bsearch(glyph_id)` compares the poisoned glyph id, and the following branch on `c` at line 1055 is where the saved report fires.

patch_analysis.patch_description: The fix adds an immediate bailout in `OT::apply_lookup()` when `buffer->move_to(match_positions[idx])` fails.

key_changes.change: Replaced `buffer->move_to (match_positions[idx]);` with `if (unlikely (!buffer->move_to (match_positions[idx]))) break;`, preventing recursive sublookup dispatch on unchanged cursor state after a failed reposition.

The unresolved part is the earlier cursor-setting history before the failed `move_to()` path.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's authoritative run on the exact staged 2786-byte witness reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `bsearch<unsigned int>` during the second `hb_shape()` call, after the witness's last 64 bytes have been copied into `text32[16]` and GSUB lookup processing reaches nested `ContextFormat3::apply` recursion.

format.name: HarfBuzz hb-fuzzer witness font plus trailing UTF-32 text
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact blob in `poc`, accepted by `hb_face_create()`. `hb-fuzzer` uses the whole blob as the font and copies its last 64 bytes into `text32[16]` for the second `hb_shape()` call. On the witnessed path, GSUB processing reaches nested `ContextFormat3::apply` / `OT::apply_lookup` recursion and the fix-relevant OOM-handling path at `buffer->move_to(match_positions[idx])`; vulnerable code then continues into recursion on unchanged cursor and the later coverage lookup crashes in `bsearch<unsigned int>`. The saved artifacts do not record which earlier cursor-setting step made that unchanged cursor land on an unwritten `buffer->info` slot, so this contract is intentionally limited to the exact witness and sink-reaching recursion rather than a broader class of fonts or neighboring inputs.
